intro_detail: I make games, I’m interested in AI and I like 3D rendering.
selection_note: Personal projects and projects from my studies.
projects_intro: Personal projects and work from my studies. Games, web applications, 3D rendering and AI applied to physics.
spellwar_summary: A 3D game with a custom engine in C++ and OpenGL.
spellwar_detail: SpellWar is a third-person game set on floating platforms. I developed the engine from scratch.
spellwar_focus: A custom physics model, collision system, PBR renderer and terrain generation.
plants_summary: Plants generated using L-systems, with 3D rendering in WebGL.
plants_detail: This project started with reading The Algorithmic Beauty of Plants (ABOP). It was mainly about studying the ideas and putting them into practice.
plants_focus: The project brings together L-systems, maths, physics and 3D rendering in the browser with WebGL.
eyefox_summary: An Android puzzle developed during my studies.
eyefox_detail: The goal is to make two grids match. Changing a tile’s colour also changes its neighbours.
eyefox_focus: Build a puzzle around this rule and make it work on a phone.
about_body: I like code that produces striking visual results. I enjoy using maths and physics to represent a problem and learning different ways to solve it. I also care about keeping the software architecture clean.
about_outro: My work includes talking with the client, designing the product and developing it. I also handle the infrastructure, pipelines and deployment.
approach_1_body: I like designing games. One day, I’d like to make a game or tell a story with something to say.
approach_2_body: Understanding how models work and how they’re built, as well as making software that uses them.
approach_3_body: Making striking images, with the maths and physics that go into creating them.

booster_summary: Pokémon packs to open, cards to collect and trade.
booster_detail: Booster Break is a personal project that colleagues also contribute to. You can browse your collection, trade cards and prepare three-Pokémon duels. There is also a sandbox for opening packs without an account, just for fun.
booster_focus: The cards and pack-opening effects use WebGL. Behind them, a TypeScript app with React, an Elysia API and a PostgreSQL database handles collections, trades and duels. The project keeps growing through new ideas and contributions.
pinnacle_summary: Exploring activation regions in physics-informed neural networks.
pinnacle_detail: PINNacle is the starting point for this group project on explaining PINNs, neural networks trained to solve physical equations. The project visualizes their activation regions and spatial density to explore how the network represents the problem.
pinnacle_focus: I worked on extracting regions from network activations with ReLU, tanh and SiLU, quantile-based sampling and data export. I also developed parts of the C++ and OpenGL viewer to explore regions in 2D and 3D, navigate with the camera and export image sequences for video. Density statistics and heatmaps are part of the group’s work.
pinnacle_visual_caption: Illustration of activation regions in a small ReLU network. This visual is not a PINNacle training result.
dit_summary: Two image generation experiments: a StyleGAN-inspired GAN and a latent diffusion transformer.
dit_detail: This academic project explores 256 × 256 image generation with two compact PyTorch models. The GAN generates landscapes from noise. Cheap DiT learns to denoise representations of paintings in a VAE’s latent space, then converts them back into images.
dit_focus: I worked on model architecture and training. For diffusion, I moved from pixel space to latent space to reduce the sequence length processed by the transformer. The results retain visible limitations: sometimes blurry shapes, imperfect reconstructions and repeating patterns in the GAN outputs.

journey_intro: From software back to maths, following the thread of projects and experiences.
journey_engineering_body: A three-year engineering programme with foundations in algorithms, mathematics and software engineering, followed by a specialisation in image, sound and artificial intelligence. The track covers machine learning, deep learning, image and audio analysis, image synthesis and virtual reality. I put these ideas into practice through projects in games, 3D rendering, image generation and neural network explainability.
journey_work_body: At Galadrim, I designed and built custom applications from established business requirements, from technical architecture to production deployment. Working in an Agile environment, I collaborated with clients to present progress, clarify evolving requirements and explain technical constraints and trade-offs.
journey_work_branch_1: Agentic development: designing agent skills and workflows for scoping, architecture, implementation, review and validation, to accelerate development while keeping control of quality.
journey_work_branch_2: Technical guidance and mentoring: supporting developers, guiding implementation decisions and reviewing code.
journey_engineering_school: ENSICAEN · Image, sound and artificial intelligence
journey_work_employer: Galadrim · Internship from February to August, then a permanent role from August 2026
journey_work_branch_3: Delivery and reliability: cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, deployments, testing and monitoring, with attention to performance and costs.
journey_work_branch_4: My work includes an automotive parts e-commerce platform built from scratch on AWS, and gamification features for a shopping centre platform.
journey_cs_body: A year focused on computer science after my first year in mathematics, before joining the engineering programme at ENSICAEN.
journey_math_body: A first year at university focused on mathematics, the starting point of my path into computer science.
